docs.title: KU Leuven Industrial Engineering Wiki
docs.text:
Site in construction

This site is still in construction, information may be lacking or incomplete.

A student-maintained knowledge base for the Engineering Technology programmes at KU Leuven.

This wiki aims to collect study advice, course information, summaries, exam experiences, useful resources and practical guidance from students and alumni.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
This project is maintained by students and alumni.

You can contribute by:

  • Improving course pages
  • Adding study advice
  • Sharing exam experiences
  • Uploading summaries and formula sheets
  • Reporting outdated information
  • Fixing mistakes

Use the "Edit this page" button available throughout the wiki to submit improvements.

docs.title: Recommended Contributions
docs.text:
• Personal summaries
  • Formula sheets
  • Study guides
  • Solved exercises
  • Exam preparation advice
  • Software tutorials
  • Project experiences

docs.title: Please Avoid Uploading
docs.text:
• Copyrighted textbooks
  • Paid course material
  • Restricted university content
  • Material that violates KU Leuven policies

docs.title: Disclaimer
docs.text:
This wiki is an unofficial student initiative and is not affiliated with or endorsed by KU Leuven.

Information provided by contributors may be incomplete or outdated. Always consult official course documentation for authoritative information.

docs.title: Chemical Engineering
docs.text: Chemical Engineering applies chemistry, physics and mathematics to the design, optimization and operation of industrial processes. The programme combines fundamental sciences with process engineering, sustainability and industrial applications.

docs.title: Career Paths
docs.text:
Graduates work in industries where chemical, biological and process technologies play a central role:

  • Process Engineering
  • Chemical Plant Design and Operation
  • Pharmaceutical Engineering
  • Biotechnology
  • Food Engineering
  • Environmental Engineering
  • Sustainable Energy and Circular Economy
  • Materials Engineering
  • Polymer and Plastics Industry
  • Metallurgy and Advanced Materials
  • Water and Waste Treatment
  • Process Safety Engineering
  • Quality Assurance and Validation
  • Research and Development
  • Technical Consulting
  • Product Development
  • Industrial Management
  • Entrepreneurship and Technology Start-ups

Typical employers include chemical companies, pharmaceutical firms, biotechnology companies, food producers, environmental consultancies, materials manufacturers, energy companies, research institutes and governmental agencies. Graduates may also continue towards doctoral research.

docs.title: Electromechanical Engineering
docs.text: Electromechanical Engineering combines mechanics, manufacturing, energy systems, electrical engineering and control systems. Students learn how to design, analyse, automate and optimize machines, products and industrial processes.

docs.title: Stage 2
docs.text:
• Design of Industrial Control Systems
  • Applied Engineering Mechanics and Dynamics
  • Data Acquisition
  • Distribution of Electrical Energy
  • Manufacturing Technologies 1
  • Thermal Technologies
  • Systems and Control Theory
  • Engineering Experience 2 - Electromechanical Engineering

docs.title: Stage 3
docs.text:
• Machine Design
  • Electrical Machines
  • Manufacturing Technologies 2
  • Strength of Materials for Machine Design
  • Thermomechanical Machines and Installations
  • Information Management

docs.title: Design Option
docs.text:
• Operations Management
  • Aspects of Machine Design
  • Automation for Production
  • Engineering Experience 3 - Design

docs.title: Core Programme
docs.text:
• Drive Systems
  • Dynamic Aspects of Machine Design
  • Machine Learning (EM)
  • Master's Thesis Electromechanical Engineering

docs.title: Management Option
docs.text:
• Total Quality Management
  • Advanced Operations Management
  • Technology Entrepreneurship and New Business Development

docs.title: Advanced Robotics Focus
docs.text:
• Mobile Robotics
  • Modelling of Dynamic Systems
  • Control Systems and Applications

docs.title: Digital and Lightweight Manufacturing Focus
docs.text:
• Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM)
  • Manufacturing Metrology
  • 3D Printing
  • Welding and Joining Techniques
  • Lightweight Materials and Design

docs.title: Career Paths
docs.text:
Graduates can be found in a wide range of technical and industrial sectors:

  • Mechanical Design Engineering
  • Mechatronics Engineering
  • Robotics and Automation
  • Manufacturing and Production Engineering
  • Industrial Process Engineering
  • Energy Systems and Sustainability
  • Automotive Engineering
  • Aerospace Engineering
  • Medical Devices and Clinical Engineering
  • Research and Development
  • Quality Engineering
  • Technical Consulting
  • Product Development
  • Operations and Technical Management
  • Entrepreneurship and Technology Start-ups

Typical employers include manufacturing companies, energy providers, aerospace firms, automotive companies, robotics and automation integrators, engineering consultancies, research centres and high-tech product developers. Graduates may also continue towards doctoral research.

docs.title: Electronics and ICT Engineering
docs.text: Electronics and ICT Engineering focuses on electronics, embedded systems, software, communication networks, signal processing and intelligent digital systems.

docs.title: Core Programme
docs.text:
• Communication Networks
  • Digital Design Concepts
  • Computer Architectures
  • Programming Techniques
  • Systems and Control Theory
  • Analog Circuits for Signal Processing
  • Engineering Experience 2 - Electronics and ICT Engineering
  • Engineering Experience 3 - Electronics and ICT Engineering

docs.title: Smart Electronics and Software Option
docs.text:
• Operating Systems
  • Data Engineering
  • Digital Signal Processing
  • Sensors and Actuators
  • Electronic Design
  • Complex Digital Design
  • Software Engineering and Web Technology
  • Transmission of Digital Information
  • Transistor Circuits and Amplifiers
  • Introduction to Human-Computer Interaction
  • Machine Learning

docs.title: Core Programme Smart Electronics and Software
docs.text:
• Master's Thesis Electronics and ICT Engineering
  • Machine Learning (EA)
  • R&D Experience
  • Extended Reality

docs.title: Management Focus
docs.text:
• Technology Entrepreneurship and New Business Development
  • Advanced Operations Management EA-ICT

docs.title: Career Paths
docs.text:
Graduates can be found in a broad range of digital and high-technology sectors:

  • Embedded Systems Engineering
  • Electronics Engineering
  • Software Engineering
  • Full-Stack Development
  • Telecommunications Engineering
  • Network Engineering
  • Signal Processing Engineering
  • Data Engineering
  • Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
  • Cybersecurity
  • Semiconductor and Microelectronics Industry
  • Internet of Things (IoT)
  • Robotics and Intelligent Systems
  • Industrial Automation
  • Medical Technology
  • Research and Development
  • Technical Consulting
  • Product Development
  • Technology Management
  • Entrepreneurship and Technology Start-ups

Typical employers include software companies, telecommunications providers, semiconductor manufacturers, electronics firms, research centres, industrial automation companies, medical technology companies and high-tech startups. Graduates may also continue towards doctoral research.

docs.text: The General Engineering programme provides the scientific, mathematical and technological foundations that underpin all engineering disciplines. Students develop analytical thinking, quantitative problem-solving skills and a broad understanding of engineering principles before choosing a specialization.

docs.title: Career Paths
docs.text:
The General Engineering programme serves as a foundation for further specialization in:

  • Electromechanical Engineering
  • Electronics and ICT Engineering
  • Chemical Engineering
  • Biochemical Engineering

Students develop competencies that are broadly applicable across engineering disciplines, including:

  • Mathematical Modelling
  • Data Analysis
  • Programming
  • Experimental Methods
  • Engineering Design
  • Scientific Problem Solving
  • Technical Communication
  • Project Work

In the second year of the bachelor programme, students choose a specialization. The broad scientific and engineering foundation also prepares graduates for interdisciplinary projects and emerging technological fields.
